A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MMEB benchmark and VLM2Vec framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renumbered appendix tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original MMEB evaluations of trained Phi-3.5-V embedding models, dataset-level results in Appendix Table 5, and training, instruction, and task-transfer ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains original MMEB experiments and adds LLaVA results, fine-tuned baseline evaluations, candidate-count sensitivity results, and VLM2Vec results on Flickr30K. Table 11 distinguishes its cited baseline scores from the proposed model's results.

M1.justification: V1 explicitly appends and pools an EOS token; v3 specifies last-token pooling and changes Figure 3's label from EOS to LAST. Since v1's EOS was also the last token, the PDFs do not establish whether input construction changed or the description was generalized. Instruction conditioning, InfoNCE, cosine scoring, and GradCache remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The 36 MMEB datasets, four meta-tasks, and 20 training versus 16 out-of-distribution dataset assignments remain unchanged. V3 adds actual zero-shot text-to-image and image-to-text evaluation on Flickr30K in Table 11, extending coverage within an existing task family.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds UniIR CLIP SF and MMEB-fine-tuned CLIP and OpenCLIP, while retaining earlier baselines, including UniIR BLIP FF. Table 4 adds CLIP to the instruction comparison. Table 11 introduces comparisons with EVA-02-CLIP and size-specific CLIP, OpenCLIP, and MagicLens variants using cited scores. The fine-tuned controls substantially strengthen comparator coverage.

E3.justification: V3 adds MMEB fine-tuning controls for CLIP/OpenCLIP, LLaVA configurations at 336×336 and 1344×1344, candidate-count sweeps from 100 to 5,000, and Flickr30K Recall@1/5/10 evaluation. Existing MMEB evaluation counts and Precision@1 remain unchanged. The stated default batch size becomes 1,024 instead of 256, but v1's main results already used 1,024.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 and Table 5 add sensitivity to candidate-pool size, and Table 4 extends the instruction ablation to CLIP. Table 2 also compares two LLaVA image resolutions. Existing LoRA-rank, batch-size, crop-count, training-step, and meta-task-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Additional result rows and revised relative-percentage calculations introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial results for new model configurations and controls. Phi-3.5 LoRA remains at 60.1 overall and 52.0 OOD; newly evaluated high-resolution LLaVA reports 62.9 and 57.1, respectively, rather than a same-setting improvement. Appendix Table 6 replaces detailed Phi results with LLaVA results. Candidate-count, CLIP-instruction, and Flickr30K results are added; Flickr30K image/text retrieval R@1 is 80.3/94.6.

T1.justification: The instruction template, InfoNCE objective, temperature-scaled cosine similarity, and GradCache gradient derivation remain mathematically unchanged. Moving the similarity formula inline and renumbering equations introduce no new assumptions, formal results, or proofs.

C1.justification: The two central contributions, MMEB and instruction-conditioned VLM embeddings, remain unchanged. V3's introduction adds a claim of competitive zero-shot Flickr30K retrieval and distinguishes performance advantages over fine-tuned versus untuned baselines. The conclusion retains its original scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds a cost-versus-difficulty rationale for 1,000 candidates and argues that LLaVA's OOD performance is not explained by pretraining overlap. The instruction analysis now interprets contrasting CLIP/VLM2Vec behavior as evidence of VLM instruction-following advantages. V1's direct attribution of E5-V's weaker performance to text-only training is removed.

D1.justification: V3 documents LLaVA resizing configurations and the fine-tuned baseline setup. It removes v1's explicit random evaluation-sampling statement, MagicLens pure-text handling detail, and future code/data/model release commitment. The project URL and core training and hardware details remain; these edits do not establish a change in actual resource availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds Li et al. (2024), listed as LLaVA-NeXT-Interleave, and Sun et al. (2023), EVA-CLIP. It modestly revises E5-V positioning and explains why several baselines were not fine-tuned. The broader related-work coverage and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 revises the abstract and selected introductory, benchmark, baseline, and interpretation paragraphs. Experimental settings are absorbed into Section 4, subsequent subsections are renumbered, and Appendix A gains a descriptive title and roadmap. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Table 2 gains separate untuned, fine-tuned, and proposed-model groups; Table 4 gains a CLIP block and reverses the presentation of instruction effects. Candidate-count and Flickr30K tables are added. Figure 3 is relocated and relabeled, and captions are expanded. The five-figure set, example tables, and overall visual format remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: V1's central comparison lacked baselines fine-tuned on MMEB; v3 adds these controls, substantially strengthening the evidence beyond unequal training exposure. A second backbone and candidate-count analysis also strengthen generality and benchmark justification. These gains outweigh limited disclosure losses and reporting errors, including Table 6's UniIR grounding inconsistency: its listed scores average about 62.2, but the summary reports 65.3.
